rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so this is a conservative first candidate built from the contract rather than from evidence. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the body at x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 m (positive x is left), placed 0.05 m ahead of the axle so they read the line before the wheels reach it. Sensor size 0.012 m is smaller than the 25 mm tape, so the readings stay sensitive across the tape width. Wheel track 0.12 m and wheel radius 0.03 m are mid-range. Body 0.12 m wide keeps the off-track limit at about 0.06 m (tape half-width 0.0125 + 0.03), a reasonable margin. Mass 0.8 kg with a 0.18 m body length gives moderate yaw inertia. Controller: sensor_weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2] match the sensor order from right to left, so a line to the left gives a positive signal (steer left). kp = 2.5 gives strong correction without saturating the wheel commands at normal offsets. kd = 0.3 damps oscillation, and ki = 0 avoids integral windup on curves. base_speed = 1.5 gives about 75 percent PWM, enough to finish near 3 s if the robot tracks well. line_loss = last_direction so the robot searches toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with rms_error well under 0.05 m. The main risk is oscillation at the higher base speed, or sharp bends on the slalom pushing the line off the sensor array. Hypotheses to test: (1) kp is the main driver of oscillation, so steering_oscillation will rise with kp; (2) completion time is limited by base_speed, not by steering, on the gentle tracks; (3) line_loss_events stays at 0 if the sensor span covers the tape on sharp bends.
